sections.heading: Why Commercial Window Replacement Matters for College Park Properties
sections.body: College Park is a dynamic commercial environment anchored by the University of Maryland and a growing mix of retail, office, and mixed-use developments along corridors like Baltimore Avenue and Kenilworth Avenue. For property managers and building owners in this market, window performance directly affects tenant satisfaction and overall building value. Older window systems often develop seal failures, frame deterioration, air infiltration, and condensation problems that worsen over time. Replacing failing windows with modern, properly fitted glazing systems can improve thermal performance, reduce noise transmission, and give your facade a clean, updated appearance. Delaying replacement can lead to more extensive damage to surrounding framing, interior finishes, and mechanical systems, ultimately increasing repair costs. Proactive replacement keeps your building competitive in a market where tenants and visitors expect well-maintained, professional-looking spaces.

sections.heading: Glass Types and Window System Options
sections.body: Commercial glazing projects call for a range of glass types and framing systems depending on the building type, location, and intended use. Insulated glass units, also known as IGUs, are commonly used in commercial replacements because they consist of two or more panes sealed together with an insulating air or gas-filled space, helping moderate interior temperatures. Low-E coatings applied to glass surfaces can reduce solar heat gain and help maintain more consistent interior conditions. Some properties benefit from laminated or tempered safety glass depending on the application and location within the building, particularly in high-traffic areas or large glazed openings. Storefront systems, curtain wall sections, and ribbon window configurations each present unique structural and aesthetic considerations. Our team works with property managers and general contractors to identify the right glass and framing combination for each project, balancing performance, durability, and appearance.

sections.heading: The Commercial Window Replacement Process
sections.body: Every commercial window replacement project begins with a thorough assessment of the existing window systems, frames, and surrounding construction. Our team measures each opening carefully, evaluates the condition of sills, headers, and adjacent materials, and identifies any underlying issues that should be addressed before new glazing is installed. Once the scope is defined, we source appropriate glass and framing components and schedule installation to minimize disruption to building occupants and operations. During installation, existing windows and frames are removed, openings are prepped, and new systems are set, shimmed, sealed, and secured according to proper glazing practices. Final inspection of each unit ensures proper operation, weathertight sealing, and appearance. We clean up thoroughly and confirm that all replaced windows meet the agreed specifications before considering the job complete.
